title: Albo's 'Cobargo moment' as he's heckled and booed by passing locals
text:
By Nick Wilson for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 23:53 GMT, February 13, 2025 | Updated: 00:29 GMT, February 14, 2025
Anthony Albanese has been upset and booed by activists from wind farms that told him that “he went home” while greeted the followers on the southern coast of NSW.
The prime minister visited a Bluescope SteelWorks Center on Friday at Lake Illawarra to announce the working candidate for Whitlam.
But the encounter and greeting descended to chaos after it was kidnapped by anti-offshore winding parks activists who protested the event.
What is happening there? Why don’t we put them in your fucking place? Put them in front of your bloody mansion, ‘a man shouted.
Another man told Mr. Albanese to “return home.”
“Don’t respect the regions, we don’t want your wind farms,” ​​he said.
“Get out of here Albo, we don’t love you here.”
The incident has been compared when the then Prime Minister Scott Morrison was upset when he greeted the locals in the city of Cobargo, devastated by forest fires.
Anthony Albanese has been upset and booed by activists from wind farms who told him that “he went home” while greeted the followers on the southern coast of NSW
What is happening there? Why don’t we put them in your fucking place? Put them in front of your bloody mansion, ‘a man shouted (in the photo)
In images of the now infamous encounter and green, Mr. Morrison can be seen taking the hand of a firefighter who had said he did not want to shake his hand.
A person told Mr. Morrison that he should be “ashamed of himself” and said he had “left the country to burn”, while another called him “Mutt.”
Albanese looked flawed with the interruptions to their press conference while the men continued to boo from only meters away.
“Enchanted to have you friend here,” said Albanese.
The hecklers began again when the prime minister said that “he had his back” of the blue neck works in the steel industry.
‘My message is clear what’ we have my back ‘. We support the blue neck jobs, ” he said.
“Another lie,” one of the men shouted.
The Illawarra Windfarms have been subject to hot debate since the plans were revealed for the first time by the Albanese government in June last year.
Local activists are furious, claiming that the project, originally planned to feed 1.8 million homes throughout the state, would cloud the views of the coast and endanger local marine life.
Alex O’Brien, president of Future Illawarra responsible, was one of those who took the opportunity to confront Mr. Albanese.
“Our group came here because we heard that the prime minister was going to be here, and the Labor Party has continued to reject the opportunity to talk to our community about the wind farm on the high seas,” he told Sky News.
That said, his concerns seemed to have been heard when, last year, the Federal Government reduced the wind zone proposed by a third and agreed to move it more to the high seas.
Shortly after, the Norway Equinor firm and its Australian partner Oceeneex discarded their plans to develop the project.
